result: The four candidate causes were separated. (1) RELIEF is live but was misdescribed: reform is a joint condition on relief AND cross-shore distance and distance binds -- the loop's own 0.90 m of relief reforms when spread over 30 m instead of 15, giving surf zones at 360-388 m and 453-500 m with 65 m of calm between. (2) DECAY RATE is the same axis (the e-folding count is K*L/d); reform needs K ~ 0.35-0.40 against the flux-form standard 0.15. (3) NO MEMORY is dead: the transform marches the flux and carries gamma_b/gamma_s hysteresis, proved by --bug no-hysteresis and by the probe row. (4) FORCING HISTORY is dead and reverses: storm/calm cycling, +-0.5 and +-1.0 m semidiurnal tide, and 3/5/8-quantile Rayleigh height distributions ALL lower the relief; steady monochromatic forcing is the most favourable case this model has. (5) THE GRID, added on a parallel builder's question, is also dead: refining space and time together (dt at 0.6 of the slope term's diffusion bound dx^2/(2*6.7e-4)) the trough minimum runs 0.4574 / 0.4607 / 0.4629 / 0.4625 at dx = 2.0 / 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25 m -- converged and moving AWAY from 0.40, while the relief converges downward 0.62 / 0.52 / 0.48 / 0.44 m. Every mechanism tried trades trough width against relief, which is why the 14 per cent gap is robust rather than marginal.

closed_forms.saturated_surf_ratio: DERIVED THIS WAVE: Gamma_eq = gamma_s/sqrt(1 + (5/2)(dd/dx)/K), the fixed point of the Dally march with the shallow-water flux substituted. A broken wave on a SHOALING bed decays to a ratio strictly above gamma_s, 0.477 on this scene's inner slope (measured 0.4748). Verified against the marched transform on plane slopes 1:150-1:60 to 3 per cent, and corroborated by Raubenheimer, Guza & Elgar (1996), who measured saturated H/h at 0.2-1.0 positively correlated with local bed slope -- a field paper neither side was written from.
closed_forms.saturation_slope_limit: DERIVED THIS WAVE: tan(beta)_crit = 2K/5 = 0.060 (1:16.7), the slope above which the closed form's denominator vanishes and no saturated surf zone exists -- the shoaling gain outruns the breaking loss and the wave surges. Lands within a factor of 1.5 of Wright & Short's reflective/intermediate boundary, so the breaker-type classifier and the wave-decay model are not independent statements.
closed_forms.reform_criterion: DERIVED THIS WAVE: G(d) = G_eq + (G_c - G_eq)(d/d_c)^-a with a = K/m + 5/2, G = (H/d)^2, m = dd/dx down the back of the bar. The exponent carries K/m, so the decay is paid for in TRAVEL DISTANCE and not in depth gained. Checked against the marched transform bisected on relief across L = 10-75 m; the closed form runs a systematic 0.15-0.25 m optimistic because it assumes a straight back slope and shallow water.
closed_forms.breaker_index: unchanged and now measured in ONE depth field: d_bar/(H_b/gamma) = 0.973 at dx = 1 m and 0.981 / 0.973 / 0.982 / 0.992 across dx = 2.0 / 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25 m.

overturned: WAVE 1's OWN d_bar/(H_b/gamma) = 0.893 AND ITS FALSIFIABLE TREND ARE WITHDRAWN. The comparison straddled two depth fields -- H_b and d_b come out of the transform, which reads the wavelength-filtered depth, while cr['d'] is the raw bed, and the 1.5 m filter lifts an 11 m crest by 0.19 m. In one field the ratio is 0.973. Refining the grid, the raw form climbs 0.852 / 0.893 / 0.940 / 0.971 while the same-field form does not move; the sea-state trend is the same curve along a different axis, because a bigger bar is a broader bar and a fixed filter takes proportionally less off it. A parallel builder reached the same conclusion independently from the discretisation. Chapter 12's d_bar ~ H_b/gamma is met to 1-3 per cent and is NOT asymptotic.

gamma_s = 0.40 is not the H/d a surf zone relaxes to. It is the FLAT-BED limit of a slope-dependent family, Gamma_eq = gamma_s/sqrt(1 + (5/2)(dd/dx)/K). A chapter naming gamma = 0.78 as the breaking index should not let a reader infer a second constant a broken wave decays to.

Chapter 12's 'the profile breathes on a storm/calm cycle' does not build a wider bar in 1-D -- it builds a LOWER one. Storm/calm cycling, tidal cycling and a Rayleigh height distribution were all measured and all reduce the relief, because a moving break point smears the flux convergence into a terrace. The breathing is real as a statement about bar MIGRATION; read as a mechanism for bar RELIEF it is backwards.

break_lines() was being read as 'the breaking lines' and it is the ONSET test. H/d >= gamma marks where a wave starts breaking and says nothing about where one stops, so on this profile it returns a single 1 m interval and empty space over a 140 m band of white water. surf_zone_spans() reads the transform's own hysteretic state and is what section B's criterion is about.

Wave 1's 5*pi/16 was filed under 'overturned' as if chapter 12 carried a wrong coefficient. The chapter carries no coefficient at all -- it writes V_long proportional to ... and stops -- so it is an ADDITION to the chapter, not a correction. Settled by a parallel builder this wave; recorded so nobody inherits a phantom disagreement.

The embayment is an OUTPUT of chapter 12's coastal loop run in plan with a spatially varying hardness: corr(shoreline, hardness) = -0.95, amplitude 55 m on 189 m of mean retreat, and the same loop with hardness set to 1 leaves 0.45 m of amplitude against 45.6 m with it -- the chapter's 'uniform rock gives a straight cliff and nothing else', run as an experiment. Bound 0.513 at d = 1.7 m with d_ref the 8 m shelf; measured regression slope 0.366.
closed_forms.breaker_index: d_bar/(H_b/gamma) = 0.935 +- 0.028 across 89 independent cross-shore profiles that the coastal loop shaped differently from one another, both terms in ONE depth field. Widening notchHeight restarts the retreat and destroys the bench, so the chapter's own platform diagnostic and its retreat loop are in conflict as written. The missing term is UNDERCUTTING, which a heightfield cannot hold (chapter 11's representation warning, which 12 already invokes for arches); its heightfield expression is that waves attack the first land cell above the waterline. With it, both halves of the diagnostic work.

ITS DEPOSITION STEP LOSES THE ROCK IT ERODES. beach = (1 - exposure)*nearShore is identically zero over open water, where the fetch sweep saturates, and LARGEST on the dry plateau, where the sweep returns zero because no fetch reaches a cell behind a cliff. Measured: 116154 m^3 lost out of a closed domain in one version, and the shoreline stalled at 0.4 m of retreat in another. Three corrections and none is a coefficient -- the band is water, the material stays in the row it came from (moving it alongshore IS longshore drift), and the fill is capacity-limited at the datum with the excess exported and reported. 90 per cent of the debris leaves, which is what a real cliff does with it.

NOTHING IN THAT SECTION LIMITS THE PLATFORM'S WIDTH: 235 m of bench and still widening at 1600 steps, because nothing attenuates the wave crossing it. The feedback is the chapter's own breaking index -- the wave reaching a cell is min(H_0, gamma_b*d) and the work goes as H^2 -- so a cliff behind a wide shallow bench is attacked by a small wave. Added at NO new constant.

THE DALLY DECAY CARRIES AN OBLIQUITY AND THE CHAPTER'S 1-D FORM IS THE OTHER ONE. dF/dx = -(K/d)(F - F_s) with F = E c_g cos(theta) applies the rate per unit cross-shore distance; the divergence form a plan view needs applies it per unit ray distance. gap: Bar section A's BACKLIT WAVE FACE cannot be rendered from this representation, and the reason is geometric and provable rather than a shortfall of effort. A ray entering water is confined to the Snell cone, so a sightline that travels ALONG a crest -- which is what a backlit face is -- needs the face tilted at least 90 - asin(1/n) = 41.48 deg from the horizontal. This scene's linear free surface eta = (H/2) cos(S) reaches |grad eta| = 0.1443 over the whole bay, which is 8.21 deg: six times too gentle. Section A therefore belongs beside section F's plunging lip, one step EARLIER and for the same structural reason -- the height field is not the obstacle at breaking, it is already the obstacle at steepening. The shortest route to closing it is named: beach.py already computes the wave skewness Sk from the Ursell number and spends it only inside the sediment transport, never on the free surface. Not attempted this wave. The frame that carries section A is therefore the bar's OWN instrument -- a variable-path cuvette of this scene's water in this scene's sun -- and its caption says it is a stand-in. result: FIRST IMAGE OF WATER IN THIS PROJECT, and every number in it measured in scene-linear before the tone map. THE COLOUR IS THE PATH, measured on the TRANSMITTANCE so the source spectrum cancels: 2G/(R+B) runs 1.0000 at zero path, 1.1420 at 1 m, 1.4518 at 2.9 m. The grade thick/thin is 1.355 backlit and 1.348 front-lit -- IDENTICAL, because the grade is the path and the path does not know where the sun is. The face against the body is 1.382 / 0.961 = 1.44: the wedge at 2-3 m of path against the same water seen as a body with no path at all. What separates backlit from front-lit is the FORWARD GLOW, chapter 28's own term: the same HG lobe reads 0.6215 /sr at 15.8 deg and 0.0019 at 159 deg, so the glow is 5.07% of the backlit pixel and identically 0.00% of the front-lit one, with only the observer moved. THE IOPs ARE NOT INVENTED: chlorophyll's amplitude a_ph(440) = 0.1083 m^-1 is RECOVERED from chapter 28's own Jerlov 1C entry through Gordon's K_d relation and round-trips; the HG asymmetry g = 0.9132 is DERIVED by requiring the lobe to backscatter exactly the chapter's 1/51; the mineral load is a Bagnold balance on the BED's stream power, not a slider. THE GLITTER IS THE SLOPE DISTRIBUTION: at U10 = 6 m/s (Cox & Munk mss 0.03348) the path is 14.96 deg wide in the near field and 6.63 deg at the horizon -- it NARROWS by 2.26x toward the horizon while brightening 14x, which is bar section K's own prediction -- and width/sqrt(mss) is constant to 1.7% over a factor of five in wind, which is what makes it a readout rather than a look. SIX FINDINGS, three of them overturning: (F1) the suspension must be Rouse-STRATIFIED or a physically correct load renders the whole Atlantic as Jerlov 5C -- green reflectance 0.038 two-layer against 0.158 depth-averaged at 8 m, a factor of four, and it is what separates a blue offshore from a milky one; (F2) the forward glow is NOT Beer-Lambert -- it goes as L exp(-cL) -- so 5% of forward-scattered light biases a cuvette inversion by -24.3% IN THE GREEN, the band the whole colour argument lives in, while the transmitted term alone inverts to 0.00%; (F3) 10.3% of the flux the surface intercepts reflects BELOW the horizon and a single-bounce glitter model drops it; (F4) Cox & Munk's component fits sum to 0.003 + 5.08e-3 U and their own combined fit is 0.003 + 5.12e-3 U -- 0.8% apart, and a file that quotes both as if one implied the other has misread the source; (F5) chapter 28's '550-570 nm window' is a statement about the WATER, not the pigment -- a_ph alone minimises at 592 nm and what sits at 550-570 is the minimum of a_ph PLUS pure water; (F6) the shared modules would not stretch in two places -- atmosphere.sky() reads a module-global SUN_DIR so a second scene cannot supply its own sun, and optics.rho_water and its slab integrals take a SCALAR depth where a beach's depth is a field. Neither is a physics error and neither cost a result; both are interface friction only a SECOND scene could expose, which is the argument for having built one. AND ONE DEFECT THIS WAVE SHIPPED AND NOW GUARDS: the glitter's branch -- the eye is opposite the sun's azimuth, not under it, and written the other way round the whole path evaluates at exp(-135). A glitter model with the wrong branch renders BLACK rather than wrong, which is the kind of defect that survives a look at the picture.

The steepening asked for was delivered -- the surface stopped being a sinusoid and the steepest face went 8.23 -> 15.78 deg, x1.95 -- and it does not reach the 41.48 deg = 90 - asin(1/n) a lengthwise in-water sightline needs. The reason is a THEOREM and not this scene: Stokes' 120 deg corner (1880) caps EVERY wave of permanent form at a 30 deg face -- deep-water Stokes at any order, cnoidal, solitary alike -- because a stagnation crest forces q ~ r^(1/2) and a wedge flow of interior angle 2a has q ~ r^(pi/2a - 1), so 2a = 120 deg with no depth, wavelength or height in it. 30 < 41.48. Section A requires the wave to be within about 11 deg of overturning, which is the multivalued instant bar section F puts out of scope: A AND F ARE ONE CRITERION AT TWO MOMENTS, and the gap between them is 11.48 degrees. Measured r/(2Ur) = 1.0033 at the shallowest cell and r/(ak/2) = 1 in the deep limit. ONE NONLINEARITY, TWO MOMENTS: Sk = (3/4) r cos(psi)/((1+r^2)/2)^(3/2) and As = -(3/4) r sin(psi)/(...), so Sk^2 + As^2 is a function of r ALONE and psi merely rotates between them; psi = -(pi/2) f_brk carries the same harmonic from a bound peaked crest to a pitched-forward bore using the breaking fraction the transform already has, with BOTH endpoints derived (a bound harmonic is phase-locked; a bore is a sawtooth) and only the interpolation declared. Seven new deliberate defects, every one caught: fov-on-the-long-side 11 rows, landscape-not-upright 12, dip-unrefracted 7, separation-small-angle 5, hfov-scaled-linearly 1, flat-sea-no-horizon 1, and bubble-fresnel-one-channel 3 in --bugs-foam. EVERY CAMERA PARAMETER HAS AN ABSOLUTE ROW, including the depression's own UNCERTAINTY -- without a row on the interval a future wave could narrow it silently and be claiming evidence it does not have.
result: THE THREE CAMERA PARAMETERS COME FROM THREE DIFFERENT PIECES OF EVIDENCE AND SAYING WHICH IS WHICH IS MOST OF THE VALUE. (1) THE FIELD OF VIEW IS QUANTIZED BY THE INSTRUMENT and is the best determined: the bar names an iPhone 16 Pro, a chord seen from p chords back subtends 2 atan(1/2p) with THE CHORD CANCELLING, so 'the whole embayment from its own rim' fixes the FOV without a map or a scale. The widest lens is 89.9117 deg across upright against the 90.00 that half a chord back needs -- so the instrument BOTH selects the 0.5x ultrawide (106.175 x 89.912 upright) AND proves the photographer stood at least 0.50077 chords back. A bound on where a person was standing, from a spec sheet. (2) THE DEPRESSION is the only parameter the picture measures and without the pixels it is BRACKETED: 25.455 +/- 13.296 deg for J, 27.805 +/- 12.761 for K. One measured horizon row -- 0.0263 deg per row at the phone's own 4032 -- collapses it to +/- 0.13 deg, a factor of a hundred from one number nobody has extracted. And a content fact that was expected to bind DOES NOT: 'dune vegetation in the foreground' gives delta > -50.8 deg, because an upright 106 deg frame held LEVEL already contains the ground at the photographer's feet. (3) THE EYE HEIGHT IS NOT MEASURED BY THE HORIZON. The dip is 0.123 deg at 17 m and 0.278 at 90 m -- a sixth of a degree between a low cliff and a high one, inside a hand-held tilt error, with sensitivity falling as 1/sqrt(z). WHAT DOES MEASURE IT is the resolved surf-line separation atan(z/(D-s)) - atan(z/D), and it has a closed-form ceiling DERIVED HERE because no source states it: the maximum over z is at z* = sqrt(D(D-s)), the GEOMETRIC MEAN of the two ranges, where tan(d_max) = s/(2 z*). At D = 704 m that is 682 m, so a cliff is always on the linear branch. Fed this scene's own surf-zone width it demands an eye at 25.0-102.1 m against the 17.31 m this bed supplies. REFRACTION_K is fitted to Bowditch's dip table (1.757 arcmin per sqrt m) rather than declared.

closed_forms.the lens from a ratio: a chord W seen from a perpendicular standoff p subtends 2 atan(W/2p); expressing p as a multiple of W removes W entirely, so the required field of view is a function of the ratio alone and the bay's size never enters the inference.
closed_forms.the separation ceiling: d(z) = atan(z/(D-s)) - atan(z/D) = atan(zs/(D(D-s)+z^2)); dd/dz = 0 at z* = sqrt(D(D-s)) with tan(d_max) = s/(2 sqrt(D(D-s))). DERIVED, not cited -- no source states it. Checked against a 20001-point scan over five decades of eye height.
closed_forms.the dip: acos(R_eff/(R_eff+z)) on R_eff = R/(1-k); geometric 1.9261 sqrt(z) arcmin, refracted 1.757 sqrt(z), which is Bowditch's tabulated dip and is what k = 0.1678 is fitted to.
closed_forms.the flat-sea cost: dip - atan(z/far) = 0.1229 - 0.0258 = 0.0971 deg, the band of sky the render paints sea over, with 23.7 km of fictitious ocean compressed into it.
closed_forms.the disc-average internal reflectance: an impact parameter uniform over the DISC is a cosine weighting over the hemisphere, so the disc-average of the internal Fresnel reflectance IS the diffuse internal reflectance -- optics.R_INT = 1 - (1-R_EXT)/n^2 by reciprocity, recovered by a quadrature sharing no code with it to seven digits in all three bands.

overturned: WAVE 6's BUBBLE TRACE EVALUATED ALL THREE CHANNELS AT RED'S REFRACTED COSINE. Found by a chapter builder verifying it independently. optics.fresnel broadcasts a scalar cosine to three channels, so the array shape was right and the energy sum still closed -- R and (1-R) were consistent with each other AT THE WRONG ANGLE -- and only the red band landed on anything. A wrong ANGLE per channel is invisible to every shape and energy check in the file. Fixed per channel, the disc-average recovers optics.R_INT to seven digits in all three bands (0.473713/0.476167/0.480681 against 0.473712/0.476166/0.480681), which is now the strongest row in the foam section. b_b/b moves 0.0230 -> 0.0233; wave 6's twentyfold finding is untouched. TWO ABSOLUTE ROWS MOVED WITH IT, 0.11% each, and EVERY RATIO ROW IN THE SECTION SURVIVED THE DEFECT UNCHANGED -- the fifth time in this project an absolute row was the only thing that could have seen a defect.

WAVE 7'S OWN FIRST VIEWPOINT, and it was wrong in the direction the inference invites. The eye-height instrument says the frame wants height, so the first `viewpoint` walked inland looking for it -- and produced a frame 64% coastal plain from 58 m back. On a straight 0.08 ramp, inland buys 8 cm of height per metre of standoff and spends a whole metre, so the sea's angular extent shrinks the whole way and past 60 m the ramp occludes its own brow. The correction finds the brow as a SLOPE BREAK; the wrong version is recorded in the README because 'stand higher' is exactly what the next reader will try.

THE SEAM MEASUREMENT'S OWN FIRST DRAFT. horizon_check samples the frame's outer columns, which is right for a frame aimed down the sun (the edges are 15-17 deg off the path) and WRONG for frame J, whose left edge lands within 3 deg of the sun. It reported the sea-sky seam as 6188% off continuity, which was the glitter path. horizon_seam chooses its columns by their actual azimuth from the sun.
marked_open: THIS BED CANNOT SUPPLY BAR J'S EYE HEIGHT. The resolved surf lines demand 25.0-102.1 m and wave 3's coastal loop leaves a brow at 17.31 m with a straight ramp behind it that occludes itself. A statement about the coastal loop, not about the camera.

THE AIR BETWEEN THE CAMERA AND THE SEA IS NOT MODELLED. No extinction along the line of sight and no airlight scattered into it, over frames 38-40 km deep. The Rayleigh half needs NO new constant (beta = atmosphere.TAU_R / 8.5 km = 1.19e-5 /m green); the aerosol half is `?` and is reported as a 20-60 km visibility bracket through Koschmieder. It is the CHEAPEST high-value item on the gap list because it is also what closes the sea-sky seam.

THE DEPRESSION'S OWN INTERVAL, +/- 13.3 deg, carried as a row so nobody narrows it silently. It is a read off an image this repository does not have. What would collapse it is named: one measured horizon row.

THE ILLUMINANT FOR THE CLIFF FRAMES. J and K carry no time, but J's colour ladder -- deep blue offshore grading to teal -- is a FRONT-LIT sea, and the bar's own two timed cliff frames are 56.22 deg / 123.13 deg. The render's 21.02 / 273.75 is 35.2 deg lower and 209.4 deg round, and the bar's warning is that a wrong quadrant leaves the elevation correct and is otherwise silent. Moving it means re-deriving all four of atmosphere.py's illuminants, which is a wave.

THE SEA AT GRAZING READS AS HARD SHORE-PARALLEL BANDS. The resolved free surface carries only the swell, mss 0.0013 against Cox & Munk's 0.0335, and the missing 96% is carried statistically for RADIANCE and not at all for SILHOUETTE. Invisible in every earlier frame because none of them looked at water at grazing incidence. Not a call to add noise.
